patch_description: Add sparse outgoing and incoming neighbor-service factors. For each node, estimate how well each possible neighbor can serve destinations (or origins) using a balanced demand-affinity profile. Score each neighbor pair for coverage and load balance, then decompose that score into link-level linear preferences and a sparse residual interaction. This targets the competition between the two links available at each node, rather than simply rewarding more two-hop paths. The pair budget is set independently of factor strength, at about n/3 per node and direction, keeping the added coupling count modest while also providing energy differences useful for ranking valid topologies and exchanges.
